brazil_top50_people.method: person = first listed author of the cited corpus work (family name + first initial, accents dropped); count = distinct Brazilian theses citing a matched work by that person; before = matched by existing crosswalks; after = plus works recovered by this layer. Consolidation (lc-cluster, edition-split) does not change these counts.
brazil_top50_people.brazil_theses_note: denominator = 2,615 Brazilian theses with at least one strict citation (2,618 strict BR theses in dissertations.csv); the round-1 hand-back wrongly said 12,000+ (that is roughly the whole corpus, 13,996 strict theses)

reasons: imprint strings parsed as titles ("Rio de Janeiro: Paz e Terra, 1988" 30 theses; "São Paulo: Companhia das Letras, 1995" 28): no title to translate
História social do jazz (20+5): LC catalogues The jazz scene under Hobsbawm's pseudonym Francis Newton, so the same-author check fails (held, correct by the rule)
misspelled author "Hobsbawn" (several works): the family name does not match LC
chapters/introductions ("Introdução: A invenção das tradições") and edited volumes (História do marxismo, Storia del marxismo ed.) without a matching main entry
Ranger co-author string parsed as a title ("& RANGER, Terence")

check_hobsbawm_brazil.note: kg_after counts person = first cited author (family + initial) of matched works; the parsed-name route counts every corpus work the corpus parser credits to hobsbawm|e*, matched or not; the remaining 3.5-point gap is the unmatched remainder above, not a counting difference

check_compilations_person_credit.finding: At corpus (parsed-name) level the author already gets the citation: data/field-research/dissertation-citations-2026-10-11/authored.csv.gz credits e.g. bourdieu|pierre with W:bourdieu|o poder simbolico. In the KG, a compilation has no canonical work, so it has no Work node and no CITES edge; the author loses those citations at person level unless the graph carries them another way.
check_compilations_person_credit.carried_in: compilations.csv.gz now has corpus_person_key and kg_person_key (the KG person who authored most of that corpus person's matched works; share given) for 113 of 121 rows; e.g. O poder simbólico -> p-1129 Pierre Bourdieu, Microfísica do poder -> p-422 Michel Foucault, A história cultural -> p-1213 Roger Chartier
check_compilations_person_credit.proposal: export: mint an unkeyed Work node per compilation (id corpus:<work_id>, kind compilation, resolution unkeyed) with CITES from the citing theses and a linked_authored edge to kg_person_key (linkage table, not identity evidence, as for the cited-works layer); never a canonical/edition link

not_judged.note: the second group cannot pass the LC route at all (only the key-log-work route); the first is the tail of cited 5-6, left for a later round from the same frozen index
